At the end of 2024, utility-scale string inverter assembly had the largest manufacturing capacity at around 9.5 GW , followed by central inverters (9 GW ) and MLPE ac ac (7 GW ). Inverter manufacturing has a significant percentage of U.S.-headquartered companies. ac There are Japanese, Israeli, and European manufacturers as well. In 2024, many MLPE inverters were produced in the United States, while most central inverters (which represented 80% of 2024 U.S. inverter shipments) came from Europe and China. Domestic PV inverters cost more to produce and have higher market pricing compared with inverters made elsewhere owing to higher material and labor costs as well as various incentives. Power transistors are key components of PV inverters. MLPE started using metal-oxide- semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) around 2019. MOSFETs are faster and more efficient at lower voltages than transistors used for larger applications. Historically, larger inverters have used insulated-gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs), but they are beginning to switch to SiC MOSFETs, because MOSFETs are more efficient with the higher-voltage module strings that are increasingly common in U.S. PV systems. Power electronics manufacturers in the United States generally specialize in SiC or GaN transistor technologies, but some domestic PV inverter manufacturers have supply agreements that, given the manufacturing locations of their suppliers, have a high probability of sourcing transistors from Germany and Malaysia. Printed circuit board assemblies (PCBAs) are specified components within the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) safe harbor table for the investment tax credit domestic content bonus, which has helped drive demand for domestic PCBA suppliers. Medium-voltage transformers (defined in this report as having high-side voltages of 1–69 kV) are another critical electrical product used in large-scale PV applications, which step-up the ac voltage supplied by the PV system to be fed onto the grid. There is a global supply shortage of all transformers due to growing demand from renewable energy, electric vehicles, and data centers combined with a slow build-out of supply. The resulting transformer shortage has lengthened product lead times and increased prices. In 2024, developers were expected to wait 1–2 years for smaller step-up transformers and up to 3–5 years for larger step-up transformers, and the delays could increase if projected demands outpace expanded supply. It is estimated that around half of medium-voltage transformers deployed in the United States are made domestically. Domestically produced medium-voltage transformers cost approximately 10%– 25% more than imports. Over half of large medium-voltage transformers imported came from Mexico in 2024, and imports from South Korea and Colombia grew significantly.
